extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer-review researchers, and clinicians interested in peer review quality
extracted.subtask_description: Randomized controlled trial measuring how blinding reviewers to author identity and requiring signed reports affect the quality of peer review, using a manuscript with seeded weaknesses as the test instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of weaknesses commented on (main outcome measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of weaknesses in the paper that were commented on by the reviewers (stated as the main outcome measure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary quantitative measure of review quality; reported means were 2 (with subgroup means 1.7, 2.1, 1.8, and 1.9 for groups 1, 2, 3, and 4 and 5 combined, respectively). There were no statistically significant differences between groups in this metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to reject (reviewer recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviewers recommended rejection of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an outcome reflecting reviewers' overall judgment; reviewers who were blinded to authors' identities were less likely to recommend rejection than those aware of authors' identities (odds ratio 0.5; 95% CI, 0.3-1.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate of detection of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The rate at which reviewers detected errors/weaknesses in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as an indicator of report quality; study conclusion: neither blinding reviewers nor requiring them to sign reports had any effect on the rate of detection of errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding reviewers to authors' identities (double-blind vs single-blind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviewers received manuscripts with authors' names and affiliations removed (blinded) or were aware of authors' identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented by allocating reviewers to groups where groups 1 and 2 were blinded while groups 3 and 4 were aware. Effect on primary outcome: no significant change in number of weaknesses identified, but blinding was associated with lower likelihood of recommending rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requiring reviewers to sign their reports (accountability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviewers were asked to sign their reports versus returning them unsigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented by asking groups 1 and 3 to sign reports and groups 2 and 4 to return reports unsigned; group 5 was the journal's usual anonymous request. The intervention showed no effect on the number of weaknesses detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of being in a study (observer effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviewers knew they were taking part in a study or were unaware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group 5 differed from group 4 only in that its members were unaware they were taking part; this condition tests potential behavior change from study awareness (no specific difference reported in abstract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a manuscript with seeded/introduced weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifying a paper accepted for publication by introducing a set number of known weaknesses (eight) to provide an objective test of reviewers' ability to detect problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodological choice provides a ground truth against which reviewer comments are measured (number and type of weaknesses detected).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer response (participation) rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of invited reviewers who returned reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports were received from 221 reviewers (53% response rate); response rate is relevant for interpreting representativeness and possible bias in measured outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of peer review reports (overall concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: The general concept of peer review quality, motivated by concerns about 'anxiety about bias, lack of accountability, and poor quality of peer review' and operationalized via detection of weaknesses/errors and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study treats quality as detection of manuscript problems and appropriateness of recommendations; conclusion states that neither blinding nor signing is likely to improve the quality of peer review reports.
